_doc: THE DECLARED container-vs-anchor classification for `wip-lanes.js::refCensus`.
WHY A DATA FILE AND NOT A LIST IN THE CODE. The census answers a question with
a destructive consumer: a ref classed `container` is work somebody is expected
to drain, and a sweep built on a wrong classification deletes a contract anchor.
That judgment is a DEPLOYMENT's to make, not this library's, so it is declared
here and overridable (see `loadRefPolicy`: an injected `policy` object, the
`COC_REF_POLICY` env var naming an alternate file, or editing this file).
THE THIRD VERDICT IS THE POINT. A ref matching no rule below is NOT a container
and NOT an anchor — it is `unclassified`, counted in its own bucket and folded
into neither total. `instrument-discipline.md` MUST-1: a classifier that
defaulted unknown refs to either verdict would emit the same answer whether or
not it had ever seen the ref, and a reaper reading `container` off that default
is one `--apply` from destroying something nobody classified.
EVIDENCE, not invention. The `containers` prefixes below are the namespaces
MEASURED holding work on this repo in the 2026-09-11 container audit (694
containers; 49 of 50 tags were work containers, one was a release anchor). The
`anchors` entries are the classes that audit found must NOT be swept — chiefly
`refs/tags/provenance-event-schema/v1`, which has ten live references including
a shipped fixture whose `schema_tag` field IS that string, so a blanket tag
sweep would have broken a cross-repo contract anchor.
GLOB SEMANTICS are deliberately IDENTICAL to `bin/remote-ref-reap.mjs`'s
`globMatch`: `*` is the only metacharacter and expands to `.*`, so it DOES
cross `/`. There is no `**`, because inventing a second dialect for the same
job is the drift this corpus refuses. Patterns match the FULL refname
(`refs/tags/x`), never the short form — git shortens `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`
to a bare `origin`, which would enter a sweep as a branch named for the remote.

refs/heads.reason: a local branch is a lane: unlanded work that exists on exactly one machine

refs/remotes.reason: a pushed lane is recoverable but still unlanded; MUST-8 counts every remote

refs/stash.reason: a stash is work in the one container with no branch-shaped surface reporting it

refs/tags.reason: MEASURED 49 of 50 work containers and 1 release anchor — neither default is honest, so each tag is matched against the rules below and is `unclassified` if none fires

refs/notes.reason: git notes are metadata attached to existing commits; they hold no unlanded work

refs/coc.reason: the COC coordination substrate (`hooks/lib/coc-sign.js`); a trust surface, not a lane

_doc: THE DECLARED ADJUDICATION WINDOW, read by `bin/check-archive-adjudication.mjs`.
WHY IT IS HERE AND NOT A CONSTANT IN THE CHECKER. The `containers` list below
classes `refs/archive/*` a container with the reason "615 refs measured live on
this repo in the 2026-09-11 audit". That is a COUNT, not a policy: it says the
namespace holds work and says nothing about when somebody must decide what the
work IS. A container with no deadline only grows, and the 2026-09-11 content
adjudication measured what that costs — of the 95 archive refs that were not
ancestors of `dev`, 68 were already landed (pure noise), 18 were DROP, 8 were
LANDABLE and 1 was UNKNOWN. ~7% held real inventory; the other 93% cost a full
adjudication pass to discover. The one unrecoverable item was an UNREVIEWED WIP
rescue parked so long nobody could say what was in it — the second-order cost of
deferring the verdict, not of keeping the ref.
The window is the missing half of that classification, so it belongs on the same
declared surface a deployment already overrides (see `loadRefPolicy`: an injected
`policy` object, `COC_REF_POLICY`, or editing this file). `loadRefPolicy` reads
only `namespaces`, `anchors` and `containers`, so this key is inert for the hook
census and cannot change any classification.
30 DAYS IS INHERITED, NOT INVENTED. It is the corpus's standing period constant —
`trust-posture.md` MUST-4 s cumulative window is 30 days — on the same reasoning
`unadjudicated-escalation.mjs` gives for taking its threshold of 3 from that rule
rather than picking a number. A window nobody can trace to an existing constant is
a number somebody argues with; this one has a precedent.
GLOB SEMANTICS are the dialect declared at the top of this file and implemented
identically in `bin/remote-ref-reap.mjs::globMatch` and
`bin/check-archive-adjudication.mjs::globMatch`: `*` is the only metacharacter, it
expands to `.*` and DOES cross `/`, and the pattern matches the FULL refname.
A REF MATCHING NO WINDOW IS NOT EXEMPT. The checker reports it `NO-WINDOW` and
REDS. An unclassified ref is exactly the case that must not read as clean — the
third-verdict discipline this file's own `_doc` already argues for.
TO A CONSUMER READING THIS FILE: the window below is DECLARED here and ENFORCED
nowhere in your checkout. MEASURED with `sync-tier-aware.mjs::buildLaneClassifier`
against a control that discriminates (`rules/security.md` returns copy/tier_match
on the same lanes): THIS FILE is copy/always_include on all seven lanes, while
`bin/check-archive-adjudication.mjs` is skip/no_tier_match on all seven. So you
hold the declaration and not the instrument. That is deliberate — the checker is a
loom-internal gate, not a shipped obligation — and it is stated rather than left to
be discovered, because a window nobody told you was unenforced reads as a promise.
If your repo archives refs and you want the deadline, the checker is a single file
with no dependency beyond `hooks/lib/git-subprocess-env.js`.
THE WINDOW EXPIRING NEVER DELETES ANYTHING. The checker REPORTS; it has no
`--apply`. An archive ref is a recovery copy and the same 2026-09-11 audit found
one whose content exists nowhere else. What expires is the SILENCE, not the ref.

windows.reason: a recovery ref written by `bin/remote-ref-reap.mjs --apply` before it deletes a remote branch; 30d is the corpus's standing period constant (`trust-posture.md` MUST-4), after which an un-adjudicated ref is LOUD

anchors.reason: namespaced contract/schema version anchor — e.g. provenance-event-schema/v1, which ten live references depend on
a remote's default-branch pointer, not a lane

containers.reason: reaped-lane parking; measured in the 2026-09-11 audit
